Key messages

    The journey, door to door

    –median days from origin port to SAM
    Departs origin portArrives at SAM
    Ocean transitVessel dischargePort and customsTo SAM

    Port and customs, step by step

    Vessel dischargedCustoms release

    Vessel discharge is shown as its own block in the journey; these steps start once the container is discharged. Each step is the median number of days from discharge to that milestone, minus the previous one, so the steps add up to the port-and-customs median. A document created before discharge counts as ready at discharge. Responsible parties as defined by the logistics team. The Excel dates have no time of day, so a step done the same day counts as 0.0 days; the "same day" column shows how often that happens.

    How each invoice type behaves

    7a. Port backlog projection

    Backlog and customs pace: last 4 weeks and next 14 days

    Solid = what happened. Dashed and lighter bars = projection. Release pace is the 7-day average of customs releases per day.

    Backlog today by days waiting

    How the projection works

    Each day, the projected backlog = previous day + containers expected at MX port (ETA_Port_Update, not yet arrived) − the release pace. The real backlog for past days counts containers that had arrived at port, were not yet released and not yet delivered on that date.

    7. Current Port Backlog

    ATA_Port exists and Customs_Release_Date is blank

    4a. In vs out

    In = containers arriving at MX port. Out = containers delivered to SAM.

    3. Critical Material Exposure Days

    Positive = days past the goal date. Negative = days of margin.

    6. Material Urgency, weekly trend

    Weekly cohort by ETA_Port_Update. Composite = urgency events ÷ (3 × containers). Click a week to see its containers.
